discovery: Prediction and discovery of correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials, moire superlattices and unconventional superconductivity
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so interactions should dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers built such devices with a simple tear-and-stack technique and found correlated insulating states and superconductivity whose phase diagram resembles that of the cuprates. The idea is simple, and the experiment opened a field. Twist angle became a new control parameter for quantum materials. A single, gate-tunable, clean device can now be driven through correlated insulating, superconducting, magnetic, nematic and Chern states. Twistronics has spread to transition-metal dichalcogenides and multilayer graphene, and laboratories around the world have used it to observe fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and other phases. Few recent discoveries have given condensed-matter physics such a versatile and widely reproduced experimental platform.
